description: Prodanovic, Veljko at The Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia publishes multispectral plant-health and soil-moisture observations in bioretention systems through Co-UDlabs. A low-cost Plant-o-Meter camera is tested on real stormwater biofilters under artificial irrigation. The study treats soil moisture as a proxy for retention and pollutant-removal behaviour, aiming to inform maintenance needs in nature-based drainage systems. Coverage is Co-UDlabs OTHU bioretention experiments; the inspected description does not list exact dates or sampling intervals. Zenodo provides a data ZIP with descriptive DOCX and equipment documentation with free access under CC BY 4.0. These observations support the source-defined drainage measurement, physical-model or simulation activity. Related Co-UDlabs experiments describe other assets and test conditions; they are not assumed to be independent or interchangeable measurements. A limitation is plant-health and moisture correlations are proxy evidence and do not by themselves measure pollutant removal or prove transferability to every green roof. Only native metadata and file descriptors were read; no data values, archive, code or report body was obtained.
